first_impression.reaction: Typed 'paros wedding venues' on the train. The first line tells me the three parts of the island where the venues are, and the next line says it depends on guest count, ceremony type and whether guests stay on site. That's an answer, not fluff. The takeaways give me two real capacity numbers and a heads-up about chapels, and there's a jump list. I'd read the takeaways, glance at the table, tap Naoussa because that's the name I know, check the checklist and FAQ, then bookmark.

journey.quote: Paros wedding venues sit in three parts of the island: Naoussa and the bays of the north coast, Parikia and the hills above its gulf in the west, and Golden Beach on the east coast.
journey.reaction: Answer in the first sentence, exactly what I searched. Three areas is easy to hold in my head.

journey.quote: Choose the area first, because Naoussa and the north, Parikia and the west, and Golden Beach on the east coast each offer a different kind of venue and a different base for guests.
journey.reaction: Same three areas I just read two lines ago. First bullet is a repeat.

journey.quote: Few Paros venues publish a wedding capacity, and the clearest figures belong to Petra Farm (a chapel for 120 and an event space for 150) and The Secret View (110 for a terrace ceremony, 120 for dinner).
journey.reaction: Real names and real numbers. If I've got about 100 people, I already know two places to look.

journey.quote: Six of the eight venues have a chapel on site, but only The Secret View names a ceremony type (symbolic), so ask the others which ceremonies their chapel takes before you plan around one.
journey.reaction: Didn't know chapels might not take every kind of ceremony. Handy warning.

journey.section: Paros wedding venues at a glance
journey.quote: | Venue | Area | Type | Ceremony options | Capacity |
journey.reaction: Five columns, still a sideways swipe on my phone to reach capacity, and when I get there it's 'Not published' in six of eight rows.

journey.quote: The Secret View sets each space out separately, from 30 for a ceremony under the Pergola to 110 on the Terrace.
journey.reaction: Good, small wedding to big wedding at one place. That's useful.

journey.quote: Here you choose between a beachfront hotel with its own chapel and an estate in the hills above.
journey.reaction: Fine here, but then the Golden Beach section further down says almost exactly the same sentence again.

journey.quote: Ask for current wedding terms, as that page dates from 2018.
journey.reaction: Ha, honest. My first question is always 'is this still true?' and they've answered it before I asked.
Okay, noted. Then it's in Anemoi, Monastiri, Petra Farm, Pyrgaki and Poseidon too. I got the point in the takeaways.

journey.quote: Arriving by boat at the dock is the detail guests will remember.
journey.reaction: Okay, that's cute. Boat arrival to a beach wedding. Screenshot.

journey.quote: The farm limits itself to 10 weddings a year, and its team is on site to oversee every supplier for the whole rental period.
journey.reaction: Only 10 a year? That makes it feel special. Would send this to a friend.

journey.section: The Secret View at Fladakia Estate, above Golden Beach
journey.quote: House rules are published: loud music stops at 2am, out of respect for the local villages, with a quieter after-party (an acoustic band, for example) possible.
journey.reaction: A real rule with a real time. This is the kind of thing nobody tells you until it's too late.

journey.section: How to get married on Paros
journey.reaction: Australia again. I'm in Singapore, so this whole legal bit isn't for me.

journey.quote: Flights from Athens International Airport to Paros take about 45 minutes, and from Thessaloniki about 1 hour 15 minutes.
journey.reaction: Quick, specific. Exactly what my guests will ask me.

journey.quote: May and October sit either side of the warmest months at the Naxos station.
journey.reaction: Nice that there are actual temperatures per month, dated and sourced. But the section ends without just saying 'aim for this month'. And why Naxos? It explains, fine, but I had to read twice.

journey.quote: Ask every venue on your shortlist these questions, and get the answers in writing:
journey.reaction: This list is the bookmark. Eight questions I'd never have thought of all at once.

journey.quote: That depends on the weather you want.
journey.reaction: The FAQ is the one place I want a straight answer, and this one starts with 'it depends'.

journey.section: Shortlist your Paros venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: So it's an Australian company. Not sure they'd take me.

unanswered_questions: Roughly what does a Paros venue cost? Even a ballpark. There isn't a number on the page.
Which month should I actually aim for? I get the temperatures, but the page never just says it.
How far is each venue from the airport or from Parikia port? Only Monastiri gives a drive time (from Naoussa).
Do you work with couples outside Australia, and how do non-Australians handle the legal side?

turn_offs_found.why: The same sentence closes the Ceremony bullet at six venues in a row. The takeaways already told me chapels don't say which ceremonies they take, so skimming on my phone I keep hitting the same gap instead of what's different about each place.

turn_offs_found.quote: | Venue | Area | Type | Ceremony options | Capacity |
turn_offs_found.why: I swipe sideways on my phone to reach Capacity, the one column I care about, and six of eight rows say 'Not published'. The two numbers that exist are already in the takeaways.

turn_offs_found.quote: Choose the area first, because Naoussa and the north, Parikia and the west, and Golden Beach on the east coast each offer a different kind of venue and a different base for guests.
turn_offs_found.why: It repeats the intro I read seconds earlier. The takeaways are the bit I definitely read, so a repeat there wastes a slot.

turn_offs_found.quote: Here the choice is between a beachfront hotel with its own chapel and an estate in the hills above the sand.
turn_offs_found.why: Almost word for word the same as the Golden Beach line in 'Choosing an area of Paros'. Reading the same sentence twice makes the page feel padded.

turn_offs_found.quote: That depends on the weather you want.
turn_offs_found.why: The FAQ question is 'When is the best time to marry on Paros?' and the answer opens with 'it depends'. I came to the FAQ for a quick answer and had to read the numbers and work it out myself.

would_share_with: A friend planning a Greek island wedding; I'd send her the booking checklist and the Petra Farm '10 weddings a year' bit
My partner, for the Monastiri boat arrival

cta_reaction.why: I'm only looking, not planning yet. The links are inline, no pop-ups, and they don't nag, so they didn't bother me. I'd bookmark before I'd enquire, and the 'AUD for Australian couples' line makes me think it isn't for me anyway.

top_3_changes: Drop the repeated 'Ceremony types are not published.' line from each venue's Ceremony bullet (the takeaways and the booking checklist already cover it), and cut the near-duplicate Golden Beach sentence from either the area overview or the Golden Beach section.

Make the table readable on a phone: drop or merge the Capacity column (it is mostly 'Not published') or fold the two published figures into the Ceremony options column, so there's no sideways swipe for almost nothing.

Give 'When is the best time to marry on Paros?' a one-line direct answer before the numbers, and swap the first takeaway (a repeat of the intro) for something new, such as the booking checklist pointer or a line on when to aim for, using only what the existing weather figures support.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Priya, a casual Google searcher on a phone
No invented brand facts; missing info went to unanswered_questions
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Person-set title, deferred business details and deliberately unprinted prices not treated as must-fix; no request for sourcing lines

assumptions: Persona is provisional (weight 0.10); reactions reflect generic informational search intent.

Arrived from a Google search for 'paros wedding venues' on a phone; read the intro and takeaways, glanced at the table and compare section, skimmed the area overview, jumped to Naoussa and the north, scrolled through the other venues, then the travel, weather, checklist, FAQ and closing sections.
Prices are deliberately not printed; the missing ballpark is logged as an unanswered question only.
The Australia-focused framing (AUD, legal section) is logged as a low-severity objection and unanswered question from a non-Australian reader, not a must-fix, since business focus is deferred.
The 'month to aim for' change is limited to what the draft's existing weather figures support; no climate facts were invented.
Read with images not yet loaded; image slots and HTML comments judged as invisible.
Quotes with inline HTML fact comments, link markup or bold markers are given as a reader sees them.
